# Candakinnarījātaka (Ja 485)

**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul13.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Candakinnarījātaka* (Ja 485; also attested as *Candakinnarajātaka*) is a canonical birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection [Skilling]. According to its opening nidāna, the Buddha related this story while dwelling in the banyan grove near Kapilapura in reference to Rāhula's mother in the palace. Its prelude recounts how the Buddha's wife lived as a widow while he practiced severe asceticism, for which the Buddha praised her enduring fidelity and love [Young 2004]. The core narrative relates the story of the *kinnara* couple Candakinnara and Candakinnarī, featuring a king who, captivated by the singing and dancing of the *kinnarī*, shoots Candakinnara with an arrow to take her for himself [Fausböll 1887].

In Southeast Asian Pali literature, the *Candakinnarajātaka* is integrated into the *Bimbābilāpa* alongside the *Mahādhammapālajātaka* (Ja 447) and the *Narasīhagāthā*; this narrative is closely related to the *Bimbābilāpa-parivatta* (Chapter 19) of the *Paṭhamasambodhikathā* [Skilling].
